questions.prompt: The law of conservation of mass explains why, in a chemical reaction:
options: energy cannot be created nor destroyed, only transformed or transferred.
the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.
new atoms are created from the reactant atoms.
when rearranging atoms to form products, the mass changes significantly.
questions.explanation: Mass of reactants equals mass of products in a closed ordinary chemical reaction.

questions.prompt: Copper reacts with sulfur dioxide to form copper sulfide and oxygen gas. The reactants for this reaction are:
options: copper, sulphur dioxide, copper sulfide and oxygen gas
questions.explanation: Reactants are copper and sulfur dioxide.

questions.prompt: When petrol explodes, it releases energy in the form of heat and light. This reaction is an example of:
questions.explanation: Exothermic: energy is transferred to the surroundings as heat/light.

questions.prompt: Neutralisation reactions between acids and bases can be generalised by which one of the following word equations?
options: acid + base → hydrogen gas + salt + water
acid + base → salt + carbon dioxide + water
questions.explanation: Acid plus an appropriate base gives salt and water in the elementary neutralisation model.

questions.prompt: Which of the following chemical equations is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: HCl+NaOH→NaCl+H₂O has equal atom counts on both sides.

questions.prompt: Where organisms live together and both benefit from the relationship, the interaction is classified as:
questions.explanation: Mutualism benefits both organisms.

questions.prompt: Producers are vital in ecosystems because:
options: they recycle nutrients back into the soil
they don’t consume other living things
they make carbon dioxide and oxygen
they are the only organisms that can make food materials
questions.explanation: D is the intended school answer: producers synthesise organic food from inorganic sources, supplying the food web. Some wording is simplified; producers do not literally create energy.

questions.prompt: Look at the food chain shown. Using the information in the food chain, determine which statement is NOT a correct inference. clover  caterpillar  lizard  kookaburra
options: The kookaburra is dependent on the clover.
There would be a greater mass of kookaburras than lizards.
questions.explanation: D. Normally less biomass is supported at higher trophic levels; the simple food chain supports the other inferences.

questions.prompt: From the following lists, choose the one that only contains physical (abiotic) factors.
options: soil moisture, sunlight, air temperature, soil texture
pollination, parasitism, humidity, soil humus content
questions.explanation: C lists only abiotic factors.

questions.prompt: Your hand feels cold as an ice-block melts on it. Identify the correct explanation for this process. Heat has transferred from:
options: the ice-block into your hand by conduction.
your hand to the ice-block by conduction.
the ice-block into your hand by radiation.
your hand to the ice-block by radiation.
questions.explanation: B. Energy transfers from warmer hand to colder ice by conduction.

questions.prompt: To protect people from getting shocked, wires should be covered by
questions.explanation: A. Appropriate electrical insulators reduce shock risk.

questions.prompt: Which of the following materials is an insulator?
questions.explanation: D. Rubber is an electrical insulator in ordinary dry conditions.

questions.prompt: Heat passes through liquids chiefly by
questions.explanation: C. Bulk circulation transfers thermal energy through a liquid by convection.

questions.prompt: The standard unit for electric current is
questions.explanation: C. Electric current is measured in amperes.

questions.prompt: An electric circuit is constructed with a battery and two globes in parallel. If another globe is connected in parallel, what would happen to the brightness of the first two globes?
options: They would stay the same brightness.
questions.explanation: A. Across an ideal fixed-voltage supply, adding a parallel globe leaves the voltage and brightness of existing globes approximately unchanged.

questions.prompt: An element is a:
options: pure substance made up of only one type of atom.
pure substance made up of two types of atoms.
substance that contains no bonded atoms.
questions.explanation: Element: pure substance with one type of atom.

questions.prompt: An atom has a mass number of 27. It therefore has:
questions.explanation: B is the neutral-atom option with13protons+14neutrons=27nucleons and13electrons. Mass number alone does not identify the element; neutral is implicit.

questions.prompt: Which of the following BEST describes a neutral atom? In neutral atoms, there are always equal numbers of:
questions.explanation: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the outermost shell in an atom?
questions.explanation: Valence shell.

questions.prompt: Nitrogen is in period 2, group 15. Which of the following elements would have the most similar properties to nitrogen?
options: Sodium Na, because its symbol also starts with N.
questions.explanation: Phosphorus shares group15 and related valence chemistry.

questions.prompt: Which of the following shows the correct conjugate base pairs?
questions.explanation: Cytosine pairs with guanine in DNA; “conjugate base pairs” here means complementary nucleotide bases, not acid/base conjugates.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about the number of daughter cells produced is CORRECT?
options: Mitosis = 4 daughter cells, meiosis = 2 daughter cells.
Mitosis = 1 daughter cell, meiosis = 2 daughter cells.
Mitosis = 1 daughter cell, meiosis = 4 daughter cells.
Mitosis = 2 daughter cells, meiosis = 4 daughter cells.
questions.explanation: Typical mitosis produces2 daughter cells; meiosis4.

questions.prompt: What is the name given to an individual whose alleles are the same for a characteristic?
questions.explanation: Homozygous means identical alleles at a locus.

questions.prompt: What is the term used to describe alleles that have equal dominance?
questions.explanation: Codominance: both alleles are expressed in the heterozygote.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the energy changes occurring when an apple falls from a tree branch to the ground below?
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy becomes kinetic, with some sound/thermal energy on impact.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE regarding kinetic energy?
options: The greater an object’s mass, the greater its kinetic energy.
The greater an object’s speed, the greater its kinetic energy.
An object at rest has no kinetic energy.
questions.explanation: All three are valid under the intended comparisons with other variables fixed.

questions.prompt: The kinetic energy of a ball rolling down along a table can be calculated  using the formula Ek=½mv2. ,if the mass of the ball is 1kg and the velocity is 2ms-1: What kinetic energy does the ball have?
What is the difference between displacement and distance?
options: Distance is the metres travelled plus the direction.
Displacement must include the direction travelled.
Displacement is only the metres travelled.
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector from initial to final position; distance is scalar path length.

questions.prompt: Speed is measured using
questions.explanation: m/s is an SI speed unit; km/h is also valid but optionB wrongly says only.

questions.prompt: A car travels a distance of 100m in 10 seconds. To calculate its average speed you will need to
A tiger runs 500m east, then turns and runs 200m west.  If the total journey took 100s: the distance travelled was
A tiger runs 500m east, then turns and runs 200m west.  If the total journey took 100s: the displacement was:
questions.explanation: 500east−200west=300m east.

questions.prompt: To convert 12 minutes to seconds you would:
questions.explanation: Multiply minutes by60.

questions.prompt: A racehorse runs a race that starts and finishes at the same point.  If the race was 1000 metres, what was the displacement of the horse when it finished?
questions.explanation: The start and finish positions coincide, so displacement0.

questions.prompt: The acceleration due to gravity :
options: is the same on all planets.
changes your mass on different planets.
changes your weight on different planets.
is a number that can’t be measured.
questions.explanation: Weightmg changes withg; mass does not.

questions.prompt: A trolley with an initial velocity of 5 ms-1 attained a velocity of 25 ms-1 in 4 seconds.  The acceleration of the trolley was:
A car was uniformly accelerated from rest at 7 ms-2.  How long did it take to reach a velocity of 56 ms-1?
Inertia can be defined as:
options: the amount of matter in an object.
a tendency of an object to resist a change in its motion.
the force of gravity on an object.
when a force makes something move.
questions.explanation: Inertia is resistance to change in velocity.

questions.prompt: A skydiver glides to the ground at a steady speed of 7 metres per second.  Which statement below best describes what is happening?
options: The upward force of air resistance acting on the skydiver is smaller than the downward weight force that is acting.
The upward force of air resistance acting on the skydiver is larger than the size of the downward weight force.
The upward force of air resistance balances the downward force of gravity acting on the skydiver.
The weight force that acts on the skydiver is larger than the upwards force of air resistance.
questions.explanation: At steady downward velocity, drag balances weight.

questions.prompt: The Law of Conservation of Energy:
options: states that energy when riding to the top of a hill doesn’t change.
states that energy can be changed from one form to another.
there is no such law for energy.
states that energy cannot be destroyed but that it doesn’t change either.
questions.explanation: B is the best statement: energy can transform. Full conservation states total energy is conserved; it is not created/destroyed in an isolated system.

questions.prompt: An atom has an electron configuration of 2,8,8,1. What group would it be in?
questions.explanation: One outer electron corresponds to group1.

questions.prompt: What are the elements in group seventeen of the periodic table called?
questions.explanation: Group17 is the halogens.

questions.prompt: The mass number of an atom is the total:
options: charge on the nucleus of the atom.
number of protons in the atom.
mass of the atom expressed in grams.
number of protons and neutrons in the atom.
questions.explanation: Mass number counts protons+neutrons for an isotope.

questions.prompt: Aluminium is in group 13.   Use this information to determine the most likely charge of aluminium ions.

questions.prompt: Which product in the following chemical reaction is dissolved in solution? CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq)  CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l)
questions.explanation: ProductCaCl₂(aq) is dissolved. HCl(aq) is a reactant, not product.

questions.prompt: Which of the following equations is balanced?
questions.explanation: 2C₂H₆+7O₂→4CO₂+6H₂O balancesC,H,O.

questions.prompt: Explain why crushing solid reactants helps to increase the rate of reaction.
options: It exposes more of the solid reactant to the other reactants so there can be more reactions occurring at any one time.
It weakens the chemical bonds in the solid so that it is easier for the reaction to occur.
It helps the solid to dissolve.
questions.explanation: A. Crushing increases exposed surface area and frequency of contact; it does not generally weaken chemical bonds.

questions.prompt: The correct formula for Magnesium Nitrate is:
questions.explanation: Magnesium nitrateMg(NO₃)₂ balancesMg²⁺with two nitrate ions.
